One client for the process

Trap: reqwest::get(...) creates a new client per call: new connection pool, new TLS session, no keep-alive. Under load this is the difference between 200 and 20,000 requests/second.

GET JSON into a typed struct

error_for_status() matters: without it, a 404 page fails later with a confusing JSON parse error.

POST JSON and read the response

Retry only what is safe

Retrying a 400 or a 422 just multiplies your error rate. Retry timeouts, connection resets, 429 and 5xx — nothing else.

Stream a response instead of buffering it

Parse JSON leniently and strictly in the same codebase

deny_unknown_fields is the right default for an API you control: a typo in a field name becomes an error instead of a silently missing value.

Produce JSON without a struct

json! is fine at the edges. Inside a hot path, serialise a struct — the macro builds a Map per call.

Read a huge JSON file without loading it

Works for JSON Lines and for a top-level array only if you use StreamDeserializer with Deserialize on each element — for a real 2 GB array, prefer JSONL.

Timeouts that actually fire

A Client timeout covers the whole request; tokio::time::timeout covers a step you are waiting on. Use both — the client timeout for the network, the outer one for your own logic.
